FXUS63 KIWX 020732
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
332 AM EDT Fri Oct 2 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Rain coming to an end across the area from northwest to
  southeast through this afternoon.

- Notably cooler today and through the weekend with highs in 
  the 60s.

- Very crisp Tuesday morning with lows in the 30s (70% chance).

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 319 AM EDT Fri Oct 2 2026

A good soaking across the area with the rain band that has been
slowly but steadily working its way through the area from the
northwest to the southeast. Many locations have already seen
near to slightly above the 1 inch rainfall mark. Here at the
office by 2 AM around 1.28 inches of rainfall had fallen so far.
The front will continue to provide light to moderate rainfall
across the area and move southeastward bringing rainfall to an
end over the northwestern portions of the CWA later this morning
and march southeastward into the afternoon. Cooler temperatures
will also arrive behind the boundary and highs today will only
reach the mid to upper 60s. This cooler and drier trend will 
continue through the weekend into next week. Highs will
generally run in the mid to upper 60s with Sunday a brief and
slight warmup with some locations especially south and east
getting into the lower 70s. Lows will also be cool with lows
generally in the 40s but Tuesday morning looks to dip into the
mid to upper 30s. Will have to watch carefully in the coming
days with a shot of clearing which will maximize the 
radiational cooling and perhaps some localized frost may be 
possible especially for the far northern and northeastern 
locations. However with the still pretty warm ground temps would
think this may be averted. Will keep an eye on that 
development. 


&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z SATURDAY/...
Issued at 119 AM EDT Fri Oct 2 2026

Cold front and associated rain band slowly progressing
southeasterly across the area overnight and will bring 
periods of scattered to widespread moderate rainfall. MVFR to IFR
cigs are likely for much of the overnight period for both TAF
sites with the boundary passage and very moist low levels. An
embedded thunderstorm or two is possible but lack of instability
should mitigate development. Rapid improvement expected later
this morning with return to VFR and clearing skies by this  
afternoon after the 20z Fri to 00z Sat time period however still
trapped moist lower levels could slow clearing.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory from 8 AM this morning to 11 PM EDT this 
     evening for LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Andersen
AVIATION...Andersen

spc.text:
SPC AC 020448

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1148 PM CDT Thu Oct 01 2026

   Valid 021200Z - 031200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorm potential is low today and tonight.

   ...Mid-Atlantic vicinity...

   An upper trough will develop eastward across the Northeast today,
   bringing some modestly enhanced midlevel southwesterly flow across
   the region ahead of a surface cold front. Showers and thunderstorms
   are likely to be ongoing along the length of the front this morning
   from the Ohio Valley to the Mid-South. Low-level warm advection
   ahead of the eastward advancing font and band of convection will
   result in persistent cloudiness across the warm sector.
   Additionally, midlevel lapse rates are forecast to remain poor. As a
   result, instability is expected to remain modest (500-750 MLCAPE)
   despite 60s F dewpoints. Deep-layer flow will largely remain
   parallel to the surface boundary, and stronger flow will lift
   northeast with time. If pockets of stronger heating can occur, a few
   strong wind gusts are possible during the afternoon from northern VA
   into southern New England. However, overall severe potential appears
   limited.

   ..Leitman/Halbert.. 10/02/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 020358

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1058 PM CDT Thu Oct 01 2026

   Valid 031200Z - 041200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe thunderstorms are expected across the U.S. on Saturday.

   ...Synopsis...
   On Saturday, a broad upper trough will develop into Ontario, with a
   leading speed max moving from the northern Plains across the Great
   Lakes. Meanwhile, an upper high will be centered over the Great
   Basin, with relatively high midlevel heights extending into the
   Southeast.

   At the surface, a high pressure center will move from MI into the
   Northeast, with the surface ridge extending southwestward into the
   southern High Plains. Northeasterly surface winds will thus relegate
   the more robust moisture/dewpoints to the Gulf Coast states.

   Isolated thunderstorms may develop during the day over the Upper
   Midwest in association with the shortwave trough, as temperatures
   aloft cool. Moisture and instability will be minimal, but weak
   elevated instability should support at least isolated lightning
   flashes.

   Otherwise, scattered thunderstorms will affect much of the Gulf
   Coast and extending into the Carolinas as the air mass will become
   marginally unstable with heating. Weak shear will further preclude
   severe possibilities.

   ..Jewell.. 10/02/2026

SPC AC 020551

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1251 AM CDT Fri Oct 02 2026

   Valid 041200Z - 051200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are not forecast for Sunday.

   ...Synopsis...
   A large-scale upper trough will continue to deepen Sunday as the
   parent low moves out of Ontario and into western Quebec. A leading
   shortwave trough will quickly move from the Great Lakes into the
   Northeast, with an attendant cold front. However, little if any
   instability will be present to support thunderstorms.

   Behind the leading wave, a secondary and stronger backside speed max
   will nose into the Upper Great Lakes late in the day, with another
   surface high building across much of the Midwest.

   Scattered thunderstorms will remain possible from the TX Coast to
   FL, where low-level moisture and instability (500-1000 J/kg MLCAPE)
   will exist. Weak shear and warm temperatures aloft will not favor
   severe storms.

   ..Jewell.. 10/02/2026
